title: Write concise public README and user guide
description:
Write a concise public-facing README.md and a user guide that accurately describe Abracapture's capabilities, build requirements, and usage. Documentation must clearly state native capture versus conversion/resampling behavior and must not promise bit-perfect capture when PipeWire negotiation or resampling is involved.

Before editing, inspect:
- The existing README.md for any content to preserve or replace.
- src/audio/PipeWireCaptureStream.hpp for capture lifecycle and format-negotiation API to document accurately.
- src/core/AudioFormat.hpp for supported formats, native-vs-converted classification, and format metadata.
- src/app/main.cpp and any CLI argument parsing for command-line usage documentation.
- CMakeLists.txt for build dependencies (Qt version, PipeWire version, libsndfile, libFLAC, ffmpeg).
- packaging/abracapture.desktop for the application description consistency.

Do not infer APIs, schemas, behavior, or file contents; inspect the referenced files first.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths.

README.md: Project overview (one paragraph), feature list, build requirements (C++20 compiler, CMake, Qt 6.11, PipeWire 0.3, libsndfile, libFLAC, ffmpeg for optional exports), build instructions (cmake configure/build/install sequence), brief usage section, and license. Keep under 200 lines.

docs/USER_GUIDE.md: Sections for: getting started (first launch, stream discovery), selecting capture sources (application streams, monitor streams, hardware inputs), capture controls (start/stop, auto-start/auto-stop, pre-roll/post-roll), output formats (WAV/FLAC masters, native format preservation, conversion disclosure), post-capture exports (lossy/lossless derived formats via ffmpeg), output directory and naming configuration, capture history, settings, and CLI automation. Include a 'Capture Integrity' section that explains: when capture is native versus quantized/resampled/converted, how the UI reports this, and that upsampled audio is not presented as higher-resolution source material. Keep under 400 lines.
acceptance_criteria: README.md exists and is under 200 lines
README.md lists all build dependencies: C++20, CMake, Qt 6.11, PipeWire 0.3, libsndfile, libFLAC, ffmpeg
docs/USER_GUIDE.md exists and is under 400 lines
User guide contains a Capture Integrity section explaining native vs converted capture
Documentation does not promise bit-perfect capture unconditionally
Documentation accurately states that upsampled audio is not presented as higher-resolution source
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: add new source files or build targets
promise bit-perfect capture when PipeWire negotiation or resampling is involved

allowed: choose documentation wording and section order
choose which CLI flags to document based on inspection
forbidden: invent features not present in the source code
add tutorial or developer contribution guide beyond scope
